title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned Circuit Schematic Blueprint. Keep it, take the alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Circuit Schematic Blueprint
options.lineage: engineering drafting — schematic sheets and blueprint diazo prints
options.thesis: The course is a layered signal path; the reviewer is its schematic sheet. Every topic is a node on one continuous circuit from the medium up to the frame, and you trace it rather than scroll past cards.
options.viewport: A full sheet: a ruled title block top-left naming the module and sheet number, a continuous signal spine running down the page with topics as tapped nodes, and the first figure already annotated with hand-drawn leader arrows into its own mechanism.
options.risk: Technical-drawing grammar can read cold and forbidding; it needs the annotation warmth to stay a study aid and not a datasheet.

raised.raise: Figures gain hand-drawn leader arrows and margin call-outs that explain the mechanism inside the drawing, instead of a caption sitting under a silent picture.
State is a mark, not a hue: a mastered topic gets a struck ink check on the sheet, a missed quiz item a grease cross in the margin. Readable with colour stripped out.
One unbroken ruled spine runs the full page — a single continuous section — instead of stacked shadowed cards, so the module reads as one signal path rather than a feed.
The vellum ground owns whole regions and cuts hard between sheets; no fades, no soft gradients, no glassy blur.
Every figure and table is labelled for literally what it is, set square on the grid — wayfinding by reading, not by decoration.

options.label: Oscilloscope Phosphor Bench
options.lineage: the instrument itself — analogue scope CRT, phosphor persistence, graticule
options.thesis: The subject's own output device: waveforms are what this course is about, so the surface that shows them is the surface's native form. Readings, traces, and measurements rather than prose in boxes.
options.viewport: One lit graticule filling the viewport, the module's signature waveform traced across it live, with measurement cursors you drag and a readout column naming what each value means.
options.risk: My own top-ranked direction, and the most familiar move in this exact category — instrument-styled technical interfaces are where most runs like this land. Charming but it can put the aesthetic before the reading.
options.case: Highest audience identification of any candidate — the scope is literally the course's instrument — and the simulators would be native to it rather than guests. It loses on dense prose: long explanatory text has no honest home on a graticule.

options.label: Copy-Shop Zine Interior
options.lineage: photocopied course handouts on coloured copy-shop stock
options.thesis: The thing the student actually holds: one typed column of argument running down a coloured sheet, the heading platen-enlarged until the letters break up.
options.viewport: One goldenrod sheet square to the frame at full size, a single 65-character typed column running its length, neighbours present only as a thin strip of their stock at the edge.
options.case: Holds BOTH axes: identification is very high (the audience reads photocopied handouts constantly) and clarity is genuinely strong — a fixed 65-character measure is excellent for dense reading. The honest cost is that its generation filter and sheet metaphor serve reading well but would fight the interactive simulators.
options.risk: The copy-generation filter can read as a novelty filter over a normal document if the stock system is not committed to.

options.label: Hand-drawn Zine Explainer
options.thesis: A friend sketching a hard concept on a napkin.
options.case: Loses on clarity for this product: marker lettering and mascot panels cost legibility on dense technical content. Kept line: hand-drawn leader-arrow annotation now lives on the blueprint's own figures.

options.label: Film Cutting-Bench Select Rail
options.thesis: A perforated rail of punched frames, the place you stopped flagged.
options.case: Loses on identification: no part of this audience's world is film editing. Kept line: state-as-mark, not state-as-colour, now marks mastered topics on the sheet.

options.label: Plakatstil Object Poster Wall
options.lineage: Berlin poster houses — flat emblem on saturated grounds
options.thesis: One product redrawn as a flat emblem across a dozen saturated sheets.
options.case: Loses on clarity: an emblem per product has no place to carry a formula or a timing diagram. Kept line: total commitment to the ground — whole regions own their colour, hard cuts, no fades.

options.label: Daylight Section Drawing
options.thesis: Daily life gathered along the moving edge of warmth through a building.
options.case: Loses on identification: beautiful, but it is a building, not a network. Kept line: the continuous unbroken section discipline, now the page's single ruled spine.

options.label: Industrial Streetwear Quote Grammar
options.lineage: stockroom textiles and hazard-stripe apparel graphics
options.thesis: Ordinary words in straight quotes with the tags left on.
options.case: Loses on both axes: the fashion register reads as costume over a technical course, and quoted caps carry no explanatory load. Kept line: literal labelling — name every figure for what it is, set square on the grid.

canonCard.label: The Standard Study Guide
canonCard.lineage: the category default for course review sites
canonCard.thesis: A clean sidebar-plus-content docs layout with a card grid for modules — what any reviewer site ships: light neutral ground, a sans stack, one accent, generous cards.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar of modules on the left, module content in a centred column, overview cards on the home route.
canonCard.risk: Predictable; it is the look every AI-generated reviewer site already has.
